record.paper_title: Absolute continuity, Lyapunov exponents and rigidity I : geodesic flows
record.original_question: Does dynamic coherence persist under perturbations of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms? More explicitly, let f be a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold with invariant tangent splitting into unstable, center, and stable bundles, written as E^u, E^c, and E^s. Say that f is dynamically coherent when there are f-invariant center-stable and center-unstable foliations tangent to E^c + E^s and E^c + E^u, respectively, and their intersections give an invariant center foliation W^c. If f is dynamically coherent, is every perturbation of f also dynamically coherent?

evidence.quote: It is not known whether every perturbation of a dynamically coherent diffeomorphism is dynamically coherent

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold and let $f : M \to M$ be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism. Recall that $f$ is partially hyperbolic if there is a $Df$-invariant continuous splitting $TM = E^u \oplus E^c \oplus E^s$ of the tangent bundle into nonzero subbundles, together with constants and a Riemannian metric such that vectors in $E^u$ are uniformly expanded, vectors in $E^s$ are uniformly contracted, and the expansion/contraction rates on $E^c$ are strictly dominated by those on $E^u$ and $E^s$, respectively. Such an $f$ is said to be dynamically coherent if there exist $f$-invariant foliations $W^{cs}$ and $W^{cu}$ of $M$ tangent to $E^c \oplus E^s$ and $E^c \oplus E^u$, respectively; in that case $W^c := W^{cs} \cap W^{cu}$ is an $f$-invariant center foliation tangent to $E^c$.

Question: Is dynamical coherence open in the $C^1$ topology among partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms? Equivalently, if $f$ is a dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism of $M$, does there exist a $C^1$-neighborhood $\mathcal{U}$ of $f$ in $\mathrm{Diff}^1(M)$ such that every $g \in \mathcal{U}$ is partially hyperbolic and dynamically coherent?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether dynamical coherence is $C^1$-open (i.e., persists under arbitrary small perturbations) among partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms appears to remain open. Examples of non-dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms have been constructed (Rodriguez Hertz–Rodriguez Hertz–Ures on $\mathbb{T}^3$; Bonatti–Fisher–Frankel–Potrie on Seifert manifolds), and many positive results hold under extra assumptions (e.g., on $\mathbb{T}^3$ or for systems isotopic to Anosov on tori/nilmanifolds), but no general counterexample showing a dynamically coherent diffeomorphism with a non-coherent perturbation, nor a general proof of openness, was found in available sources.

status_evidence.title: A non-dynamically coherent example on T^3
status_evidence.snippet: First example of a non-dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism with one-dimensional center, obtained as a perturbation of a non-partially-hyperbolic map.
status_evidence.claim: Non-dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic examples exist, but they are not constructed as perturbations of dynamically coherent ones.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical incoherence for a large class of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms on certain Seifert manifolds fail to be dynamically coherent.
status_evidence.claim: Robustly non-coherent classes exist on some 3-manifolds, but openness of coherence in general is not established.

status_evidence.title: Partially hyperbolic dynamics in dimension 3 (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing what is known about dynamical coherence and its persistence under perturbation.
status_evidence.claim: The openness of dynamical coherence in the C^1 topology is discussed as an unresolved question in general.
